items.text: REFERRED TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law and the administrative
code of the city of New York, in relation to the termination of membership in
public retirement systems
items.lawCode: Amd §645, R & SS L; amd §13-146, NYC Ad Cd
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7934             REVISED MEMO 03/12/2018

SPONSOR: BENJAMIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the retirement and social security law
and the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the
termination of membership in public retirement systems

 
PURPOSE:

Prohibits a public retirement system from requiring a member to automat-
ically withdraw from the system due to failure to work for a sufficient
number of years.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Retirement and Social Security Law to prohibit a
pension system from automatically requiring withdrawal from the system
due to a member's failure to spend an insufficient number of years as a
member.

Section 2 amends the Administrative Code of the City of New York to
repeal sections of law providing that members of the New York City
Employees Retirement System shall automatically withdraw from the
pension system due to failure to spend a sufficient number of years as a
member.

Section 3 provides for the effect date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Current law requires members of the New York City Employees Retirement
System to automatically withdraw their membership in the pension system
if they work for no more than five years, and do not return to city
service within five years after that date.

This legislation would prohibit any pension system, with particular
attention paid to NYCERS, from maintaining a policy of automatic with-
drawal due to a failure to spend a sufficient number of years as a
member. This law disincentivizes individual from returning to city
service, thus hurting the recruitment efforts of New York City in its
process to fill vacant slots and address workforce turnover. The current
provision may also violate the spirit of the New York State Constitution
by limiting the rights of a pension member to retain service credit in
the case of reemployment after the five year window.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal. Affected state employees have accrued sick leave pursuant to
their health benefit plan, and the accrual of those benefits should be
included as part of the annual OTPS appropriation for an individual
agency. The loss of this accrual is essentially a future unplanned
surplus for the state. As a result, there should be little new costs to
the state for allowing a limited number of public employees affected by
this scenario to maintain their sick leave bank to be applied to their
retiree health care cost.
 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

summary: Relates to the termination of membership in public retirement systems; provides that no public retirement system shall require a member to automatically withdraw from the public retirement system due to an insufficient number of years spent as a member of such retirement system.
